episodes.152687: A nearby front and upper air troughs generated periods of heavy rain across Oahu and Kauai. The precipitation caused ponding on roadways, and small stream and drainage ditch flooding. No serious injuries or property damage were reported.
episodes.152689: Evening showers formed over leeward sections of the Big Island as winds flowed upslope. The rain produced small stream and drainage ditch flooding, and ponding on roadways. There were no reports of significant injuries or property damage.
episodes.152696: An isolated thunderstorm moved across Hutchinson Island and into the Atlantic. The storm produced strong winds near the St. Lucie power plant.
episodes.153720: A strong atmospheric river impacted Southeast Alaska on October 26th. This was associated with a southerly jet stream that brought moisture up to Southeast Alaska from the tropics that caused widespread damage across Prince of Wales Island. Due to the effective transport of available moisture, rainfall rates with the associated storm were unusually high. This led to multiple landslides across Prince of Wales Island. Rain amounts that triggered the debris ranged from 2-3.5 in 12 hours with a near 100 year return period for a 1 hour rain accumulation. There were about 65 debris flows identified from this one event.
episodes.153823: Gale-force wind gusts were observed in the eastern Florida Straits as outflow from scattered thunderstorms moved north over the offshore waters.

events.county: Straits Of Florida From Ocean Reef To Craig Key 20 To 60 Nm Out
events.narrative: A south wind gust of 34 knots was measured and reported by the Frieghter Maersk Gateshead while encountering thunderstorm outflow while  transiting the eastern Florida Straits about 42 nautical miles east southeast of Molasses Reef Light.

events.location: 0.61 E St. Lucie Nuclear Power Plant
events.narrative: WeatherFlow site XSTL along the beach near the St. Lucie Nuclear Power Plant recorded a peak wind gust of 35 knots from the east-southeast as a strong thunderstorm exited the coast.

A very strong atmospheric river moved over western Prince of Wales and impacted areas around Craig, Klawock, Hollis, Black Bear Creek, Shaheen Creek and Staney Creek. The Klawock airport reported 3.60 of rain in 24 hours and was the 4th highest daily amount on record. Most of the rainfall fell in a short period of time and it was very exceptional from 600 AKST to 1300 AKST.  The 1 hour amount of 0.74 was a 100 year return period. The 6 hour amount of 2.13 was a 25 year return period and the 12 hour amount of 3.42 was a 25 to 50 year return period. All the rainfall produced widespread debris flows that blocked roadways on forest services roads, main highways near Black Bear Creek, between Klawock and Hollis, and Port Saint Nicholas road near Craig. There was so much runoff along with debris in the water that the Klawock water treatment plant was shut down as the reservoir was overflowing and debris clogged the intake pipes. Residence were put on a water boiling notice for a time. The city of Craig declared a disaster declaration after this event.
